OF_W with the Black knight moved h5 -> e8 (it now covers c7).
OF_W with the Black a-pawn moved a7 -> c6 (file no longer open).
Doubled rooks on the c-file; Black c6 pawn not protected by a pawn (b-pawn on b6).
OF_S with the Black b-pawn moved b6 -> b7 (it now protects c6).
Rook + minor each; Black rook and knight passive (a8, d7).
Rook + bishop v rook + knight; Black knight on e6 covers c7 (sibling of a base with the knight on e7).
Sicilian-style skeleton: White e4 knight c3 v Black d6 e5 Bg7; Black has no c-pawn (b-pawn on b7).
OP_A_W after Nd5, Black to move.
OP_A_Wp with the Black b-pawn on c7 instead of b7 (it can play ...c6).
Second skeleton: Rf1/Nc3 v Rd8/Bf8, Black pawns d6 e5, no c-pawn.
OP_B_W with the Black b-pawn on c7 instead of b7.
Bishop on f4 with open diagonals; rooks on a1/a8.

R+P v R: White rook behind its passed d-pawn (tablebase: win).
AC_BEHIND with the White rook in front of the pawn on d8 (tablebase: draw).

items.prompt: The c-file is open and Black's pieces are far away. Find the rook move that lands on the seventh rank.

claims.statement: No Black piece attacks c7.
The engine's first choice is Rc7.
Rc7 wins a pawn in the engine's best line.
The quiet alternative Kf1 is at least 0.6 pawns worse.

hints: Which square on the seventh rank can the rook reach without being captured?
Look at the c-file and at what Black's pieces can attack on c7.
The rook goes to c7. It attacks b7 and a7.
items.explain: Rc7 lands on a square no Black piece attacks, and in the engine's best line it wins a pawn. The quiet move Kf1 is at least 0.6 pawns worse.

feedback_by_move.c1c4: Rc4 stays on the file but does not use it; the entry square c7 is free right now.
feedback_by_move.g1f1: A reasonable king move, but at least 0.6 pawns worse than landing on c7.

feedback_by_move.c2c6: Rxc6? Nxc6 Nxc6: White has given a rook for a knight and a pawn. Take with the knight first.

items.prompt: The knight stands on d5 and it is Black's move. Can any Black pawn move attack the knight? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: No Black piece attacks d5.
The b-pawn can only go to b6 or b5, and neither attacks d5.
The engine rates the position at least half a pawn better for White.

hints: A pawn attacks diagonally forward. From which squares could a Black pawn attack d5?

items.prompt: White to move. White's rook stands behind its passed pawn. Is this a win or a draw? Predict, then check.

items.explain: The tablebase says White wins. A rook behind its passed pawn pushes it forward and cannot be blocked by it.
